# Results — Study 699 (Butterfly-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Bryce Gilmore / Scott Carney's Butterfly harmonic marks a reversal at D**: four
confirmed swing pivots X, A, B, C where AB retraces XA by **0.786**, BC retraces AB
somewhere in **0.382-0.886**, and a fifth point **D extends the original XA leg by
1.27-1.618x — PAST point X**, not merely back toward it (the ratio that tells a
Butterfly apart from Gartley/Bat/Crab, whose D stays inside the X-A range).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to
sibling harmonic studies [468-gartley-harmonic](../../468-gartley-harmonic/) and
[698-abcd-harmonic](../../698-abcd-harmonic/).*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 2%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Butterfly arm | AB retraces XA by **0.786 ± 0.06**; BC retraces AB in **[0.382, 0.886]** (shared XABCD structural band, not itself under test); **D = X − ext × (A − X)**, `ext` targeted at 1.444 ± 0.174 → exactly the **[1.27, 1.618]** Butterfly band, extending *past* X |
| Placebo arm | identical pivots, but each candidate's AB-retrace and D-extension *targets* are drawn uniformly at random and kept clear of the Butterfly's own bands — "any extension-and-reversal projection", seeded deterministically per candidate |
| D-touch scan | forward window of **120 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range brackets D (or closes within 0.75% of it) |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — a standard technical-signal convention, identical across arms, documented once) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0; a **random-day base-rate control** (matched bullish/bearish direction mix, 20 seeds) with Welch *t*; a **Bonferroni correction** across the pooled + 6 per-ticker 5-day tests (7 comparisons); Welch *t* for the Butterfly-vs-placebo third-axis check; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named —
not a membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Butterfly D-touch fade, pooled across the basket

Pooled confirmed pivots: **6,055** → Butterfly XABCD candidates: **89** (touched: 50,
~2 events/year pooled across all six names — this is a genuinely rare five-point
coincidence, not a signal that fires often).

| horizon | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* (vs 0) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 50 | 48.0% | +45.34  | +0.86 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **50** | **54.0%** | **+133.75** | **+2.28** |
| 10-day | 50 | 48.0% | −7.99   | −0.10 |

Hit rate (5-day): **54.0%** (Wilson 95% [40.4%, 67.0%]).

|---|--:|--:|--:|

| QQQ  | 10 | **+297.91** | **+5.39** |

| MSFT | 10 | +66.87  | +0.50 |
| TSLA | 9  | **+419.34** | **+3.34** |
| NVDA | 8  | −41.86  | −0.30 |

**SPY — the single most liquid, least idiosyncratic name in the basket — shows a
negative point estimate.** The two individually "significant" tickers (QQQ, TSLA)
are exactly the two highest-beta, most trending growth vehicles in the basket: the
kind of tape where *any* momentum-adjacent rule looks good in-sample.

## Signal axis — D-touch fade vs a random-day BASE RATE, Bonferroni-corrected

The base rate redraws, per ticker and pooled over **20 seeds**, the same number of
random entry days with the *same* empirical bullish/bearish mix as the real
Butterfly touches — the equity-drift confound a naive backtest would otherwise
credit to the pattern.

| horizon | Butterfly mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps, n=1,000) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +45.34  | −12.72 | +1.09 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+133.75** | **−24.11** | **+2.18** |
| 10-day | −7.99   | −57.28 | +0.55 |

Per-ticker, 5-day, Butterfly vs its own matched-mix base rate:

| Ticker | *n* | Butterfly mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 3  | −186.03 | −22.79 | −2.05 |
| QQQ  | 10 | +297.91 | −17.17 | +2.62 |
| AAPL | 10 | +15.85  | −52.38 | +0.74 |
| MSFT | 10 | +66.87  | −30.65 | +0.52 |
| TSLA | 9  | +419.34 | −4.05  | +2.14 |
| NVDA | 8  | −41.86  | −12.31 | −0.13 |

**Bonferroni correction across 7 tests** (the pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits,
all at the 5-day horizon — the honest price of looking at the basket seven
different ways): family-wise alpha 0.05 → critical **|t| ≥ 2.69**.

| | count |
|---|--:|
| tests clearing the naive, **uncorrected** \|t\| ≥ 2 bar | **4 / 7** (pooled +2.18, SPY −2.05, QQQ +2.62, TSLA +2.14) |
| tests surviving the **Bonferroni-corrected** bar | **0 / 7** |

Every number that looked "significant" before correction — including the pooled
headline itself — falls short once the multiple-comparison penalty for testing six
tickers is charged. This is the textbook shape of a mined result: strong-looking
until you account for how many places you looked.

## Tradability axis — the fade timer, net of costs

One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV. ~2 pooled events/year across six names —
roughly one Butterfly completion every 4-5 years per ticker.

| hold | gross | net (5 bps) | net (10 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +45.34 bps (*t*=+0.86)  | +35.34 bps (*t*=+0.67)  | +25.34 bps (*t*=+0.48) |
| 3-day  | +106.21 bps (*t*=+2.70) | +96.21 bps (*t*=+2.45)  | +86.21 bps (*t*=+2.19) |
| 5-day  | +133.75 bps (*t*=+2.28) | +123.75 bps (*t*=+2.11) | +113.75 bps (*t*=+1.94) |
| 10-day | −7.99 bps (*t*=−0.10)   | −17.99 bps (*t*=−0.23)  | −27.99 bps (*t*=−0.36) |
| 20-day | +45.16 bps (*t*=+0.31)  | +35.16 bps (*t*=+0.24)  | +25.16 bps (*t*=+0.17) |

Costs barely move any of these numbers (they're 20-50 bps events; 10 bps of round-trip
cost is a rounding error next to the point estimates) — the timer's shape, not the
cost sweep, is what kills it: the apparent edge is confined to a narrow 3-5 day
window, evaporates by 10 days, and doesn't come back by 20. Combined with the
Bonferroni result above and the ~2-events/year firing rate, there is no horizon at
which this clears the desk's certification bar.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the specific ratio pair beat a placebo?

Identical pivot pipeline; each placebo candidate's AB-retrace and D-extension
*targets* are replaced by a deterministic, seeded, off-Butterfly draw.

| horizon | Butterfly mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +45.34  | +40.67  | +0.06 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+133.75** | **+71.75**  | **+0.55** |
| 10-day | −7.99   | +178.72 | −1.33 |

Placebo candidates: **110** (touched: 36).

Per-instrument (5-day): Butterfly beats its own placebo on **4/6** tickers (QQQ,
AAPL, TSLA, NVDA) — a numerical majority, but nowhere near a statistically
demonstrable edge: the pooled Welch *t* of **+0.55** is far short of the desk's bar
in either direction. Any equal-legged extension-and-reversal projection — Fibonacci
or not — captures roughly the same thing.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA),
pooled across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample
construction); no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~46/seed | — | mean **+0.28** (sd 0.85), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.08` (seed 699) | 31 | +232.23 | **+4.30** |

The detector fires at roughly the nominal ~5% false-positive rate on the null and
lights up sharply on a planted mean-reversion tendency — the detection + inference
pipeline can find a genuine extension-and-reversal effect when one is actually
there. *(A faithful-engine / power check only; never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The pooled 5-day D-touch fade averages **+133.75 bps/event**
  (HAC *t* = **+2.28** vs zero; Welch *t* = **+2.18** vs a matched-direction
  random-day base rate) — a number that clears the naive *t* ≥ 2 bar on its own.
  But it is built from only **50 touches over 21-25 years** (~2/year pooled across
  six names), **0 of 7** Bonferroni-corrected pooled/per-ticker tests survive
  (critical |*t*| = 2.69), the 1-day and 10-day horizons show no persistence
  (*t* = +0.86 / −0.10), the most liquid name in the basket (SPY) point-estimates
  *negative*, and the pattern does **not** statistically beat a placebo
  extension-and-reversal projection (Welch *t* = +0.55). A real-looking number that
  does not survive the desk's own robustness checks.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even taking the point estimate at face value, the
  pattern completes roughly once every 4-5 years *per ticker*; the apparent edge is
  confined to a narrow 3-5 day hold and is gone by 10 days; and nothing here
  clears certification once multiple comparisons are charged. There is no regime
  in this sweep where the trade is both statistically certified and frequent
  enough to matter.
- **"Beats a random extension-and-reversal placebo?" — MIXED.** Butterfly beats its
  own placebo control on 4 of 6 tickers and at the pooled 1-day/5-day means — a
  numerical majority — but the pooled Welch *t* (+0.55) is far short of
  significance. The 0.786 / 1.27-1.618 ratio pair shows no *demonstrable*
  specificity over an arbitrary equal-legged extension; it is not clearly
  *wrong* either. Consistent with sibling [468-gartley-harmonic](../../468-gartley-harmonic/)'s
  and [698-abcd-harmonic](../../698-abcd-harmonic/)'s finding that the Fibonacci
  labels on this pattern family add no detectable information over a randomized
  ratio control.
